title: Edmund and the Wolf
premise: Kestrel Yarrow, an exiled storm-caller hiding as a charm-seller, discovers the old gods are answering prayers again because someone is feeding them stolen memories to rebuild their power. Among those memories is her own forgotten past — she was once the covenant-keeper who broke the bond between realms twelve years ago. Guided by Edmund, a boy whose prayers woke the gods, and a wolf who is actually her bound divine self, Kestrel must journey to the Sundered Altar and reforge the covenant. In the end she must choose between reclaiming her full identity as a god or remaining mortal and human, and she chooses mortality — sealing the covenant with an act of willing forgetting.
about_author: Theo Okafor is a former archivist from Lagos who writes fantasy steeped in folklore, memory, and moral ambiguity. Edmund and the Wolf is his second novel, following his acclaimed debut The Salt Cartographer's Daughter.

chapters.title: Charms for the Godless
chapters.summary: Kestrel Yarrow sells hollow charms in the magic-outlawed city of Vell, keeping her storm-calling buried. When a boy named Edmund begs her to make his sick mother's prayer 'work,' a candle flame answers him in a dead god's voice. POV: Kestrel. Emotional beat: weary caution cracking into dread and wonder.

chapters.title: The Boy Who Prayed True
chapters.summary: Edmund's answered prayer draws the attention of the Vigil, the city's anti-magic enforcers. Kestrel shelters him in her cellar shop, where he describes the voice that spoke to him — it called her by a name she doesn't recognize. POV: Edmund. Emotional beat: fear of pursuit mixed with awe at being chosen.

chapters.title: What the Wolf Remembers
chapters.summary: A grey wolf appears at Kestrel's door, unafraid, bearing a brand like her own childhood scar. It speaks only in fragments of her lost memories. The Vigil raids the shop; they flee the city together. POV: Kestrel. Emotional beat: terror of exposure giving way to hunger for her missing past.

chapters.title: Road of Small Gods
chapters.summary: On the pilgrim road, the trio finds villages where minor gods have begun answering again — greedily, wrongly, twisting wishes into curses. Someone is feeding the gods something potent. POV: Edmund. Emotional beat: disillusionment as miracles prove monstrous.

chapters.title: The Vigil's Hound
chapters.summary: Vigil captain Sorrel catches up to them; she and Kestrel share old history from the exile years. Sorrel reveals the Vigil outlawed magic not from fear but guilt over what the covenant-breaker did. She lets them go with a warning. POV: Kestrel. Emotional beat: bitter reckoning with a fractured friendship.

chapters.title: Feast of Borrowed Faces
chapters.summary: They reach the god-touched town of Ashmoor, where a feast-god grants citizens perfect false memories of happy lives. Kestrel nearly accepts one — a life without exile or guilt. Edmund pulls her back. POV: Edmund. Emotional beat: temptation and the ache of choosing painful truth.

chapters.title: The Name Beneath the Ice
chapters.summary: The wolf leads them to a frozen shrine where Kestrel recovers a sealed memory: she was the covenant-keeper who shattered the bond to stop the gods' tyranny, paying with her identity. The wolf is her severed divinity. POV: Kestrel. Emotional beat: shattering recognition — she is both victim and culprit.

chapters.title: The Hungering Choir
chapters.summary: The source of the stolen memories emerges: a cabal of god-priests harvesting minds to crown a new tyrant god. They capture Edmund, whose true prayers are the purest fuel. Kestrel bargains with minor gods for passage to the Sundered Altar. POV: alternating, anchored in Kestrel. Emotional beat: desperation hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: Sundered Altar
chapters.summary: At the altar, Kestrel confronts the rising god wearing harvested memories — including Edmund's mother's dying love, weaponized. To reforge the covenant she must merge with the wolf and become whole again, risking becoming the tyrant she once fled. Climactic battle of wills among the realms. POV: Kestrel. Emotional beat: terror of power's corruption at its peak.

chapters.title: Edmund and the Wolf
chapters.summary: Whole again, Kestral feels the old intoxication of divine power — and refuses it. She splits herself freely, sealing the covenant so gods may answer only honest, small prayers. She keeps her mortal life and Edmund's friendship; the wolf remains beside her, tamed into companionship. POV: Edmund closing. Emotional beat: bittersweet peace, identity chosen rather than imposed.
